keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Hayasa-Azzi (its Hittite shape of -1300 ends at 38.95 E, west of the area). The page gives no area; it names Kummaha, Samuha (west of Sivas, a Hittite site), Ura, the Kelkit valley and lists many modern provinces. Erzincan, Bayburt, Gumushane and Erzurum (about 44,000 km2) is the researcher's core; the Ardahan, Lake Van and Ararat fringes the page mentions as 'possibly' are not drawn.

wars.outcome: Suppiluliuma I defeated Karanni near Kummaha and made Hayasa-Azzi a vassal by treaty with Hukkana, who married his sister; the treaty forced repatriation of captives and the cession of border territory.
wars.note: The Hayasa-Azzi page marks the campaign undated; the span starts with Suppiluliuma's accession c. 1350 BC (Arzawa page) and the Suppiluliuma I page's 'early in his reign'.

notes: Cliopatria has no Hayasa-Azzi. The page is explicit that start and end are unknown, so the 1400 start and the 1200 end are bridges (the 14th century of conflict; the end of the 13th). The only anchored date is 1315 BCE (Mursili II's seventh year, from the eclipse count), from which years 8-10 are counted here. The page calls the polity a 'confederation'; it is drawn as one state at the core of four modern provinces, with no page for the Ardahan, Lake Van or Ararat fringes. Hittite vassalage is dated early in Suppiluliuma's reign by two pages, neither giving a year. The hittites dossier (me-04-a) notes the Azzi-Hayasa vassalage after Ganuvara as not drawn. Samuha (a Hittite cult centre west of Sivas) is not part of the state. The Armenian 'Hayasa' identification is the page's, not drawn on. Page budget: three pages.
